correctness.rationale: Polarity turns a line-paired outer cross-polytope into an explicit parallelotope inside the Euclidean ball. A zero-mean product distribution on its vertices gives the exact inequality sum ||w_i||^2/(alpha_i beta_i)<=1 for the dual basis. The dual vectors have norm at least one, reducing both claimed vertex bounds to sharp scalar Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities. Equality forces all dual norms to one, hence an orthonormal basis and equal radii sqrt(d). In the tight-frame clause, d line directions with a tight decomposition force orthogonality; the polar is an axis box, its Gaussian vertex measure is uniform on its 2^d vertices, and A_gamma is an explicit diagonal covariance plus a rank-one mean term. Operator monotonicity of square root and a_i^2+b_i^2=1 give the sharp sqrt(2)d trace bound. No finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: This is a motivated infinite-dimensional-family partial resolution of two explicit open conjectures from a recent geometry paper, plus the stronger linear vertex-index benchmark on the same natural class. The class is not an arbitrary parameter slice: a line-paired 2d-vertex polytope is the canonical cross-polytope combinatorial model while allowing full asymmetry along every axis. The result supplies sharp constants and complete equality rigidity, and the tight-frame clause explains the same class on the source's Gaussian quadratic side.
